name: journal-did-marcion-make-first-nt.json
content:
Marcion is called the man who made the first New Testament. The label is half right. He did bring a collection of Christian writings to Rome, and it was built around Paul. The church that rejected him then made a larger collection, and the two are easy to confuse.

What Marcion brought to Rome

Davidson dates the arrival to 144 and says: "When Marcion came from Pontus to Rome (144 A.D.,) he brought with him a Scripture-collection consisting of ten Pauline epistles."1 He left out Timothy, Titus and Hebrews. His gospel "was Luke's in an altered state."2

Davidson prints the order of the ten: "Galatians, 1 and 2 Corinthians, Romans, 1 and 2 Thessalonians, the Laodiceans, (Ephesians), Colossians, Philemon, Philippians."3 Galatians comes first, and the order differs from every later list he prints.

Davidson's reading

From these facts Davidson concludes that "external parties were the first who carried out the idea of collecting Christian writings, and of putting them either beside or over against the sacred books of the Old Testament, in support of their systems."4 Jerome, he adds, said that Marcion and Basilides denied that Paul wrote Hebrews and the pastoral letters.5

That reading puts a great deal of weight on one man. Paul's letters and the gospels were already read in churches before 144, so Marcion chose from an existing stock.6 I think Davidson is right that the church answered Marcion by collecting, and less sure that Marcion began the habit.

What the church built

The church built something larger. By the second half of the second century, in Davidson's account, the New Testament had two parts, "the gospel" and "the apostle". The first held four gospels. The second held Acts, thirteen letters of Paul and a few other books.7

The church kept four gospels where Marcion kept one, and it kept the Old Testament, which Marcion set aside.8

The pastoral letters

Marcion's list lacks the three pastoral letters. This site treats them as the work of Paul's school. Davidson says Marcion left them out "with true critical instinct", and that remark is his judgment, not a proof.9 The absence from Marcion's list is a fact worth knowing, and it is no more than that.

Verdict. Marcion made the first known collection built on Paul, with ten letters and an edited Luke. The New Testament of the churches came later, was larger and was assembled partly in answer to him.
